description: Project-neutral transport, envelope, command lifecycle, and safety boundary for opt-in AI control bridges.

scope.support_note: The envelope is versioned but experimental; embedding projects must pin an Engine revision and own their observation and action schemas.
included: UTF-8 newline-delimited JSON over a TCP byte stream
JSON-RPC-shaped request, result, and error envelopes
authorization, liveness, status, observation, event, and action methods
bounded transport, command queue, and event history behavior
loopback-first threat boundary and reference validation
excluded: a listener compiled into the FOnline core runtime
project observation fields, game action names, entity semantics, and readiness gates
MCP tool names, orchestration recipes, game-playing policies, and model prompts
server authority bypasses, administrator commands, TLS, discovery, and internet exposure

wire_rules.name: TCP byte stream
wire_rules.requirement: A bridge accepts an explicitly configured TCP endpoint; clients must not assume service discovery, TLS, HTTP, or WebSocket framing.
wire_rules.rationale: The common project implementations are local tooling channels, not an internet service protocol.

wire_rules.name: One JSON object per line
wire_rules.requirement: Each request and response is one JSON object terminated by LF; peers process lines in connection order.
wire_rules.rationale: Line framing is streamable, inspectable, and shared by both audited project bridges.

wire_rules.name: UTF-8 encoding
wire_rules.requirement: JSON lines are encoded and decoded as strict UTF-8; malformed input receives a parse error or closes the connection.
wire_rules.rationale: Project observations and action payloads may contain localized text.

wire_rules.name: Bounded line size
wire_rules.requirement: A request or response JSON payload is at most 1 MiB before the LF terminator; oversized input is rejected and the connection may close.
wire_rules.rationale: A local automation channel still needs deterministic memory bounds.

anchors: request exceeds the configured line limit

wire_rules.name: Request envelope
wire_rules.requirement: A request object carries jsonrpc=2.0, a caller-chosen id, a non-empty method string, and an object-valued params member.
wire_rules.rationale: A small JSON-RPC-shaped envelope gives correlation without claiming the full JSON-RPC specification.

wire_rules.name: Response envelope
wire_rules.requirement: A response echoes jsonrpc=2.0 and the request id, then contains exactly one of result or error; error contains an integer code and string message.
wire_rules.rationale: Strict correlation prevents one automation step from consuming another step's result.

anchors: response id does not match the request
response must contain exactly one of result or error

wire_rules.name: Sequential request processing
wire_rules.requirement: A client sends a request and consumes its matching response before reusing that connection; clients must not require multiplexing or concurrent in-flight requests.
wire_rules.rationale: The contract remains implementable by a single project-owned listener and avoids hidden ordering races.

anchors: response id does not match the request

methods.name: auth
methods.requirement: Authenticate the current connection with the configured shared token; a failed attempt leaves it unauthorized and a later attempt may succeed.
methods.rationale: Authorization state is connection-local and never inferred from a prior connection.

methods.name: ping
methods.rationale: Transport health must be distinguishable from project readiness.

methods.name: status
methods.result: {running, host, port, queuedCommands, maxQueuedCommands, events, maxEvents, observationSeq, lastError}
methods.requirement: Return transport state, queue/event occupancy and limits, latest observation sequence, and the last bridge error.
methods.rationale: Operators need bounded health information without parsing a game observation.

methods.name: observe
methods.requirement: Return the latest complete project-owned observation snapshot and its monotonically increasing replacement sequence.
methods.rationale: The envelope can be stable while every game owns its state schema.

methods.name: events
methods.requirement: Return retained events with seq greater than afterSeq in ascending order; clamp limit to 1..500.
methods.rationale: A cursor permits resumable polling without forcing observations to retain transient outcomes.

anchors: event for event in self.events if int(event["seq"]) > after_seq

methods.name: act
methods.params: project command object with non-empty type
methods.requirement: Enqueue one project-defined command and return its sequence; acceptance is not completion or gameplay success.
methods.rationale: The project client loop, not the socket thread, owns game state mutation.

error_codes.name: Parse error
error_codes.rationale: The request cannot be interpreted safely.

error_codes.name: Invalid request
error_codes.requirement: Reject a non-object, invalid envelope, missing method, or oversized request.
error_codes.rationale: Envelope failures are distinct from project command validation.

error_codes.name: Method not found
error_codes.rationale: Project action names belong inside act and are not transport methods.

error_codes.name: Invalid params
error_codes.requirement: Reject missing command type or structurally invalid method parameters.
error_codes.rationale: Malformed calls must not enter the project command queue.

error_codes.name: Unauthorized
error_codes.requirement: Reject every method except auth until the connection is authorized when a token is configured.
error_codes.rationale: A connection must never inherit authorization from another socket.

error_codes.name: Command queue full
error_codes.requirement: Reject act when the bounded project command queue has no capacity.
error_codes.rationale: Back-pressure is explicit and cannot silently discard commands.

command_fields.name: type
command_fields.rationale: The transport routes commands without owning their names.

anchors: command.type must be a non-empty string

command_fields.name: targetId
command_fields.rationale: Common convenience field; interpretation remains project-owned.

command_fields.name: itemId
command_fields.rationale: Common convenience field; interpretation remains project-owned.

command_fields.name: auxId
command_fields.rationale: Common convenience field; interpretation remains project-owned.

command_fields.name: x
command_fields.requirement: Optional project world or grid X coordinate.
command_fields.rationale: Coordinate system and units remain project-owned.

command_fields.name: y
command_fields.requirement: Optional project world or grid Y coordinate.
command_fields.rationale: Coordinate system and units remain project-owned.

command_fields.name: screenX
command_fields.rationale: Pixel origin and UI semantics remain project-owned.

command_fields.name: screenY
command_fields.rationale: Pixel origin and UI semantics remain project-owned.

command_fields.name: intArg
command_fields.rationale: A generic slot avoids transport changes for narrow scalar arguments.

command_fields.name: stringArg
command_fields.rationale: A generic slot avoids transport changes for narrow text arguments.

command_fields.name: append
command_fields.requirement: Optional request for project-defined append rather than replace semantics.
command_fields.rationale: Queue semantics are advisory until the project action handler defines them.

security_rules.name: Disabled by default
security_rules.requirement: An embedding project must require explicit configuration to start a listener.
security_rules.rationale: A control listener is a security-sensitive development feature.

anchors: compile the listener out of shipping

security_rules.name: Loopback first
security_rules.requirement: Listeners and clients default to 127.0.0.1 and refuse non-loopback operation without explicit operator opt-in.
security_rules.rationale: The protocol has no transport encryption or peer identity beyond a shared token.

anchors: non-loopback AiControl endpoints require explicit allow_remote=True

security_rules.name: Remote token required
security_rules.requirement: A sample or project listener exposed beyond loopback requires a non-empty token in addition to explicit remote opt-in.
security_rules.rationale: An empty-token remote listener is an unauthenticated process-control channel.

anchors: non-loopback listeners require a non-empty token

security_rules.name: No TLS
security_rules.requirement: Treat the shared token and all payloads as plaintext on the TCP path; use an authenticated encrypted tunnel if non-loopback transport is unavoidable.
security_rules.rationale: Token authentication is not confidentiality or replay protection.

security_rules.name: Environment-backed token
security_rules.requirement: Reference tools read tokens from a named environment variable and do not accept or print raw token arguments.
security_rules.rationale: Command lines, process listings, shell history, and reports are common secret leak paths.

security_rules.name: Compile out shipping surface
security_rules.requirement: Projects should compile the listener and remote-command path out of production clients, not merely disable them in a runtime config.
security_rules.rationale: Removing the socket and command path reduces attack and antivirus heuristic surface.

security_rules.name: Preserve server authority
security_rules.requirement: Project actions use normal client input or authenticated gameplay RPC paths; the bridge does not grant server authority or administrator capability by default.
security_rules.rationale: AI QA should exercise the same validation boundary as a player.

integration_rules.name: Project-owned listener
integration_rules.requirement: Implement the listener as an opt-in embedding-project native extension unless and until a reviewed Engine runtime owner is introduced.
integration_rules.rationale: The current protocol is reusable, but listener policy and shipping risk remain project responsibilities.

integration_rules.name: Game-loop command drain
integration_rules.requirement: The network thread only validates and queues act requests; the owning project client loop drains commands and mutates client state.
integration_rules.rationale: Game objects and script runtime state are not socket-thread safe.

integration_rules.name: Version project observations
integration_rules.requirement: The observation object carries a project-owned schema version and enough readiness/action metadata for its adapter; the Engine protocol does not define game fields.
integration_rules.rationale: Last Frontier and TLA legitimately expose different game models.

integration_rules.name: Completion event
integration_rules.requirement: Every accepted command eventually emits command_completed with commandSeq, success, and message, including unsupported or failed project actions.
integration_rules.rationale: Acceptance only proves queue insertion; agents need a correlated terminal result.

integration_rules.name: MCP adapter boundary
integration_rules.requirement: An MCP adapter may map project observations/actions into semantic tools, but its tool namespace, launch orchestration, memory, prompts, and gameplay policies are project-owned.
integration_rules.rationale: Transport compatibility must not falsely standardize one game's QA surface.

anchors: without borrowing Last Frontier or TLA gameplay schemas

integration_rules.name: Bounded queues and history
integration_rules.requirement: Command queues and retained event history have positive configured limits exposed through status; full queues reject rather than overwrite commands.
integration_rules.rationale: A stalled client loop must not create unbounded memory growth or silent command loss.

validation_rules.name: Protocol smoke
validation_rules.requirement: Run the reference client against the sample server and prove auth, liveness, status, observation, invalid input, action acceptance, completion, state update, and event cursor behavior.
validation_rules.rationale: A rendered schema alone cannot prove connection state and asynchronous lifecycle behavior.

validation_rules.name: Malformed peer responses
validation_rules.requirement: Client tests reject malformed JSON, unsupported envelopes, mismatched ids, dual result/error responses, and oversized lines.
validation_rules.rationale: Automation must fail closed instead of consuming ambiguous data.

anchors: response is not valid UTF-8 JSON
response has an unsupported jsonrpc value

validation_rules.name: Security boundary tests
validation_rules.requirement: Tests prove non-loopback refusal, per-connection authorization, wrong-token rejection, and absence of token command-line arguments.
validation_rules.rationale: Security prose must remain executable as the helper evolves.

validation_rules.name: Project native integration
validation_rules.requirement: A real project separately builds its native bridge, starts an actual client, verifies queue draining on the client loop, and checks clean shutdown/reconnect behavior.
validation_rules.rationale: The Python sample is protocol proof, not FOnline native runtime proof.

anchors: test the resulting native/script integration separately

validation_rules.name: Normal gameplay path
validation_rules.requirement: Project tests show representative actions pass through ordinary server validation and that rejected gameplay actions complete as failures.
validation_rules.rationale: A successful protocol smoke cannot prove game authorization or anti-cheat boundaries.

validation_rules.name: Shipping artifact inspection
validation_rules.requirement: Release validation confirms production clients cannot open the AiControl listener and do not contain the project remote-command implementation.
validation_rules.rationale: A disabled default is weaker than absence from the shipped binary.
